senses.sense_definition: Serving as a typical example or model of something.

examples.text: The company's success is often cited as a <w>paradigmatic</w> example of effective leadership.
Her research provides a <w>paradigmatic</w> case study for future scholars in the field.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to or constituting a paradigm.

examples.text: The shift in scientific thought represented a <w>paradigmatic</w> change in how we view the universe.
He analyzed the <w>paradigmatic</w> structures that govern the development of new technologies.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the relationship between words that can be substituted for each other in the same position in a sentence.

examples.text: In linguistics, <w>paradigmatic</w> relations contrast with syntagmatic relations in sentence construction.
The student studied the <w>paradigmatic</w> associations between nouns in the target language.

senses.sense_definition: A writer who documents the lives of religious figures as examples of excellence.

examples.text: The ancient <w>paradigmatic</w> recorded the virtues of saints for future generations.
As a dedicated <w>paradigmatic</w>, he spent his life chronicling the deeds of holy men.

traits.comment: This term is rarely used in modern English.
